newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-ROCKETS, KNICKS, JAZZ ALL TAKE 2-0 PLAYOFF LEADS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-ROCKETS, KNICKS, JAZZ ALL TAKE 2-0 PLAYOFF LEADS.

text.p: The Houston Rockets poured on the defensive pressure down the stretch Saturday and came away with a 96-84 victory over the Minnesota Timberwolves to take a 2-0 lead in their Eastern Conference playoff series.

"Our tremendous defence in the fourth quarter was the key," Rockets coach Rudy Tomjanovich said. "It wasn't one individual, but rather big play after big play from several individuals that sparked our run."
Mario Elie scored six of his 12 points in a key fourth-quarter surge that lifted the Rockets to victory and within one more win of clinching the best-of-five, first-round series.

Charles Barkley totalled 20 points and 15 rebounds and Hakeem Olajuwon added 18 points for the Rockets, who limited the Timberwolves to one basket over a 5:20 span late in the fourth quarter and displayed the late-game composure that helped them win NBA championships in 1994 and 1995.

"Everybody stepped up in the second half today," Elie said. "The difference in the fourth quarter was that we played Rocket defence and took it right to them. It was the kind of day where our defence made our offence that much more effective."

"I thought we made some key plays today," said Wolves coach Flip Saunders, steering his young team in their first ever playoff series. "They also made some key plays. They happened to make more down the stretch and that's a tribute to their experience."

Stephon Marbury scored 22 points and Tom Gugliotta added 17 for Minnesota, which led with less than six minutes to play but was held to just five points thereafter. Sixth-seeded Minnesota will attempt to avoid a sweep when it hosts Game Three on Tuesday night.
"They've never hosted a playoff game and their crowd will be a factor," Rockets guard Clyde Drexler said. "As Minnesota showed today, they're a young team with nothing to lose."

In the final minutes, the Rockets played four players in their 30s while the Timberwolves deployed Marbury, a 20-year-old rookie, and 21-year-old All-Star forward Kevin Garnett, who finished with 14 points and 12 rebounds.

The intensity of the playoffs boiled over in the fourth quarter. Wolves forward Sam Mitchell clobbered Rockets forward Kevin Willis, who had a clear path to the basket, with a swinging right forearm and was ejected.

"I'm disappointed in the way we finished, because for most of the game today we executed, played good defence and stood toe-to-toe with one of the best teams in the NBA," said Marbury. "Now we have to go home and re-focus."

In New York, Chris Childs scored seven of his 17 points in a fourth-quarter surge and the New York Knicks shut down the Charlotte Hornets for a 100-93 victory and a 2-0 lead in their Eastern Conference first-round series.
Patrick Ewing scored 30 points for the Knicks, who limited Charlotte to 3-of-16 shooting and 12 points in the last period.

"The game was ours," Hornets coach Dave Cowens said. "We just couldn't finish it off. They put pressure on us, we started missing shots, we turned the ball over again and again. And they're a good enough team to take advantage of that."
New York, which has advanced to the conference semifinals five straight years, can wrap up the best-of-five series with a win at Charlotte on Monday in Game Three.
Playing in just his second career playoff game, Childs hit three straight jumpers in a two-minute span of the fourth quarter to expand a four-point lead to 98-89 with 2:46 left.
Glen Rice scored 39 points for Charlotte, who were without starting point guard Muggsy Bogues, who aggravated a hamstring injury in Game One.

At Utah, Karl Malone scored 39 points as the Utah Jazz blew a 16-point halftime lead but recovered for a 105-99 victory over the Los Angeles Clippers and a 2-0 lead in their Western Conference first-round series.
John Stockton added 18 points for top-seeded Utah, which can wrap up the best-of-five series with a win in Game Three at Los Angeles on Monday.

Malone scored 19 points in the first half as the Jazz opened a 61-45 lead. He added 14 in the third quarter but was Utah's only offensive threat as Los Angeles, which won 28 less games than Utah during the season, roared to the lead with a 21-4 burst.
Utah reserve point guard Howard Eisley came on and made a three-point play that started a decisive 11-2 spurt for the Jazz to close the period and their downward spiral.
Lorenzen Wright led the Clippers with 17 points and Darrick Martin added 16.
